verdict.rationale: Meilisearch's first-party docs describe a native MCP server at the POST /mcp route. Through it, users can create indexes, add documents, configure settings (ranking rules, searchable attributes, faceting) and run searches with natural-language prompts. That covers operating the product, not just querying it. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that natural-language operation works in practice, and a built-in natural-language console (it relies on an external MCP-compatible AI client).

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can operate the product with natural-language commands

citations.quote: Once configured, you can create indexes, add documents, configure settings, and perform searches using natural language prompts.
Update ranking rules, searchable attributes, and faceting through natural-language prompts.
Index documents, tune ranking rules, and search Meilisearch through natural conversation in the AI client you already use.
Meilisearch ships a native MCP server at the POST /mcp route so any MCP-compatible client can search your indexes directly.
